e-382.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\int \sin x \, \textrm dx = -\cos x + C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3sin⁡x\,\text{d}x & =3\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(-cos⁡x)+C \\  & =-3cos⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\int \csc x \cot x \, \textrm dx = - \csc x + C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (-csc⁡xcot⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =-\int (csc⁡xcot⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(-csc⁡x)+C \\  & =csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

e-384.problem: Calculate the integral $\displaystyle{\int} (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x.$
e-384.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\int \sec^2 x \, \textrm dx = \tan x + C
$$

and

$$
\int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm dx = \sec x + C.
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\eqalign{
		\int (2\sec^2 x + \sec x \tan x )\, \textrm{d}x& = 2 \int \sec^2 x \, \textrm{d}x+ \int \sec x \tan x \, \textrm{d}x \
										&=2\tan x + \sec x + C.

}
$$

e-385.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\int \csc^2 x \, \textrm dx = -\cot x + C
$$

and

$$
\int \csc x \cot x \, \textrm dx = -\csc x + C.
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int csc⁡x(csc⁡x+3cot⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int {csc}^{2}⁡x+3csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x+3\int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-cot⁡x-3csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\int cos⁡y\,\text{d}y=sin⁡y+C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int 5cos⁡y\,\text{d}y & =5\int cos⁡y\,\text{d}y \\  & =5(sin⁡y)+C \\  & =5sin⁡y+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

∫(cos⁡x−sin⁡x)dx=

a
2sin⁡x+C
b

sin⁡x+cos⁡x+C

sin⁡x−cos⁡x+C

decision.explanation: Integrating term by term, ∫cos(x) dx = sin(x) and ∫−sin(x) dx = cos(x). Thus the result is sin(x) + cos(x) + C.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-cos⁡x+C, \\ \int cos⁡x\,\text{d}x & =sin⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (cos⁡x-sin⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int cos⁡x\,\text{d}x-\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =sin⁡x-(-cos⁡x)+C \\  & =sin⁡x+cos⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

∫(2cos⁡x+3sin⁡x)dx=

a
2cos⁡x−3sin⁡x+C
b
3cos⁡x−2sin⁡x+C
c
3sin⁡x−2cos⁡x+C
d
2sin⁡x−3cos⁡x+C
e
2sin⁡x+3cos⁡x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integrating term by term gives 2sin(x) − 3cos(x) + C, since cosine integrates to sine and sine integrates to negative cosine.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-cos⁡x+C, \\ \int cos⁡x\,\text{d}x & =sin⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2cos⁡x+3sin⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =2\int cos⁡x\,\text{d}x+3\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2sin⁡x+3(-cos⁡x)+C \\  & =2sin⁡x-3cos⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Since the derivative of sec(θ) is sec(θ)tan(θ), the integral is 5sec(θ) + C.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\int sec⁡\theta tan⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta =sec⁡\theta +C.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int 5sec⁡\theta tan⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  & =5\int sec⁡\theta tan⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =5sec⁡\theta +C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integrating term by term, 4sin(x) gives −4cos(x), and −3csc(x)cot(x) gives 3csc(x). Thus the integral is −4cos(x) + 3csc(x) + C.

after.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-cos⁡x+C, \\ \int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4sin⁡x-3csc⁡x\,cot⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =4\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x-3\int csc⁡x\,cot⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =4(-cos⁡x)-3(-csc⁡x)+C \\  & =-4cos⁡x+3csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Sec²(x) integrates to tan(x), and −2csc(x)cot(x) integrates to 2csc(x). Thus the integral is tan(x) + 2csc(x) + C.

after.name: Question 13
after.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-csc⁡x+C \\ \int {sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =tan⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int ({sec}^{2}⁡x-2csc⁡xcot⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int {sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x-2\int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =tan⁡x-2(-csc⁡x)+C \\  & =tan⁡x+2csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14

Calculate ∫sec⁡x(7sec⁡x+4tan⁡x)dx.

a
−7tan⁡x−4csc⁡x+C
b
−7tan⁡x+4csc⁡x+C
c
7cot⁡x−4sec⁡x+C
d
7cot⁡x+4sec⁡x+C
e
7tan⁡x+4sec⁡x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Expand the integrand to 7sec²(x) + 4sec(x)tan(x). These terms integrate to 7tan(x) and 4sec(x), giving 7tan(x) + 4sec(x) + C.

after.name: Question 14
after.worked_solution:
Recall that

$$
\begin{aligned}\int sec⁡xtan⁡x\,\text{d}x & =sec⁡x+C, \\ \int {sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =tan⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int sec⁡x(7sec⁡x+4tan⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int (7{sec}^{2}⁡x+4sec⁡xtan⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int 7{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int 4sec⁡xtan⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =7\int {sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x+4\int sec⁡xtan⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =7tan⁡x+4sec⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-csc⁡x+C \\ \int {sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =tan⁡x+C.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int (4csc⁡xcot⁡x+{sec}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & =\int 4csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int {sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =4(-csc⁡x)+tan⁡x+C \\  & =-4csc⁡x+tan⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\int sin⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-cos⁡x+C, \\ \int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-cot⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$

Question 20
?

Calculate ∫csc⁡x(3cot⁡x+2csc⁡x)dx.

a
−3csc⁡x−2tan⁡x+C
b
3csc⁡x−2sec⁡x+C
c
−2cos⁡x+2tan⁡x+C
d
3sin3⁡x−2cot⁡x+C
e
−3csc⁡x−2cot⁡x+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Expand to 3csc(x)cot(x) + 2csc²(x). These integrate to −3csc(x) and −2cot(x), giving −3csc(x) − 2cot(x) + C.

after.name: Question 20
after.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-cot⁡x+C, \\ \int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int csc⁡x(3cot⁡x+2csc⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int (3csc⁡xcot⁡x+2{csc}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 3csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int 2{csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x+2\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(-csc⁡x)+2(-cot⁡x)+C \\  & =-3csc⁡x-2cot⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Recall that

∫csc2⁡xdx=−cot⁡x+C,∫csc⁡xcot⁡xdx=−csc⁡x+C.

Therefore, we get

∫csc⁡x(3cot⁡x+2csc⁡x)dx=∫(3csc⁡xcot⁡x+2csc2⁡x)dx=∫3csc⁡xcot⁡xdx+∫2csc2⁡xdx=3∫csc⁡xcot⁡xdx+2∫csc2⁡xdx=3(−csc⁡x)+2(−cot⁡x)+C=−3csc⁡x−2cot⁡x+C.

Recall that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-cot⁡x+C, \\ \int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x & =-csc⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int csc⁡x(3cot⁡x+2csc⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int (3csc⁡xcot⁡x+2{csc}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 3csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x+\int 2{csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int csc⁡xcot⁡x\,\text{d}x+2\int {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(-csc⁡x)+2(-cot⁡x)+C \\  & =-3csc⁡x-2cot⁡x+C.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
